problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vehicle. The available containers are:
* Container 1: volume 16 m³, revenue 279 credits
* Container 2: volume 4 m³, revenue 65 credits
* Container 3: volume 25 m³, revenue 60 credits
* Container 4: volume 27 m³, revenue 75 credits
* Container 5: volume 31 m³, revenue 300 credits
* Container 6: volume 20 m³, revenue 207 credits
* Container 7: volume 1 m³, revenue 282 credits
* Container 8: volume 3 m³, revenue 121 credits
* Container 9: volume 11 m³, revenue 100 credits
* Container 10: volume 30 m³, revenue 101 credits
* Container 11: volume 29 m³, revenue 107 credits
* Container 12: volume 1 m³, revenue 268 credits
* Container 13: volume 50 m³, revenue 33 credits
* Container 14: volume 33 m³, revenue 250 credits
* Container 15: volume 32 m³, revenue 208 credits
* Container 16: volume 18 m³, revenue 242 credits
* Container 17: volume 22 m³, revenue 288 credits
* Container 18: volume 42 m³, revenue 60 credits
* Container 19: volume 49 m³, revenue 97 credits
* Container 20: volume 37 m³, revenue 30 credits
* Container 21: volume 29 m³, revenue 258 credits
* Container 22: volume 31 m³, revenue 146 credits
* Container 23: volume 28 m³, revenue 125 credits
* Container 24: volume 49 m³, revenue 33 credits
* Container 25: volume 3 m³, revenue 177 credits
* Container 26: volume 25 m³, revenue 258 credits

The vehicle has a maximum cargo capacity of 452 m³. Choose the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
